findings.highlight: I've returned to the state I was in the day before yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 一昨日、寝る前に届いた雪菜のメールを、まだ開けないままの自分がここにいる
findings.explanation: Haruki says Setsuna's message arrived before he went to sleep the day before yesterday and remains unopened now. The English says he has returned to an earlier state in which he could not read it before sleep, obscuring the continuing deliberate silence that he is confessing.
findings.japanese:
だから、一昨日、寝る前に届いた雪菜のメールを、
まだ開けないままの自分がここにいる。
findings.todokanai: That's why I've returned to the state I was in the day before yesterday, back when I was unable to bring myself to read Setsuna's text before I fell asleep.

findings.highlight: performed in high school back when I was in my fourth year
findings.evidenceJa: 例の付属祭でやった『雨月山の鬼』…四年の時あれ見て
findings.explanation: Uehara saw Chiaki's play at the affiliated high school's festival while he himself was a fourth-year university student. The English places his 'fourth year' in high school, producing a nonexistent school year and blurring the joke that he is now a seventh-year university student.
findings.japanese:
「例の付属祭でやった『雨月山の鬼』…
四年の時あれ見て思いっきり引き込まれてね。
彼女が大学に進学してくれたときは歓喜したよ」
findings.todokanai: "I was deeply fascinated when I watched The Demon of Mt. Uzuki being performed in high school back when I was in my fourth year. I must admit I was really delighted when I heard she was enrolling at this university."

findings.highlight: an up-and-coming company
findings.evidenceJa: 新進座のオーディションで内定出ててね
findings.explanation: 新進座 is the company name, Shinshinza, and Chiaki had already received an offer through its audition. The English treats the name as the adjective 'up-and-coming,' directly conflicting with the next line's description of it as a huge, top-tier company.
findings.japanese:
「当時、新進座のオーディションで内定出ててね。
危ないところだった」
findings.todokanai: "She refused the unofficial offer of an up-and-coming company after an audition. It was a close call."

findings.highlight: she got approval from those concerned
findings.evidenceJa: 関係者にもらったって言ってたけどな
findings.explanation: Uehara says Chiaki claimed to have received the audio source from someone involved. The English says she received approval, pre-empting the separate licensing discussion and breaking Takeya's immediate realization that he was the insider who supplied the recording.
findings.japanese: 「関係者にもらったって言ってたけどな」
findings.todokanai: "I heard she got approval from those concerned."

findings.highlight: I was the first one, you know
findings.evidenceJa: あたし、初めてだったんだよ？
findings.explanation: Chiaki tells Io that it was her own first time, then stresses that she gave Haruki everything he asked of her. The English says Chiaki was 'the first one,' which reads as a claim about being Haruki's first partner and reverses the vulnerable evidence she adduces for loving him.
findings.japanese:
「言っとくけどね、あたし、初めてだったんだよ？
あいつに求められたこと、何でもしてあげたんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "For the record, I was the first one, you know? I managed to give him everything he so desired, didn't I?"

findings.highlight: You were lying only to get close to him
findings.evidenceJa: 最初から騙すつもりで春希に近づいたんだよね
findings.explanation: Io says Chiaki approached Haruki from the beginning with the intention of deceiving him. The English says she lied in order to get close, reversing means and end and weakening Io's accusation that the intimacy itself was planned as part of the deception.
findings.japanese:
「だってあんた、好きだから騙した訳じゃないよね？
最初から騙すつもりで春希に近づいたんだよね？」
findings.todokanai: "After all, you didn't lie to him because you loved him, right? You were lying only to get close to him right from the start, weren't you?"

findings.highlight: the sigh that escapes my mouth does nothing but rise gently into the sky
findings.evidenceJa: そのため息をつく口は、結構端が上がっていたりしてた
findings.explanation: While cursing providence for drawing them together, Haruki admits that the corners of his mouth were often raised in a smile. The English makes the sigh itself rise into the sky, erasing the bodily evidence that he secretly enjoyed the supposedly unwanted bond.
findings.japanese:
俺はその天の采配を神に呪いつつ、
けれどそのため息をつく口は、
結構端が上がっていたりしてた。
findings.todokanai: I curse whatever powers above may be that are responsible for this, but the sigh that escapes my mouth does nothing but rise gently into the sky.

findings.highlight: "Oh dear, oh dear～ You're really naive, aren't you, Haruki? It's not like I said I'd dump you or anything～"
findings.evidenceJa:
「やっだな～も～。
本当にナイーブなんだから春希は。
別にふってないってのに～」
findings.explanation: ナイーブ means emotionally sensitive or delicate here; the English false friend 'naive' makes Chiaki call Haruki gullible.
findings.japanese:
「やっだな～も～。
本当にナイーブなんだから春希は。
別にふってないってのに～」
findings.todokanai: "Oh dear, oh dear～ You're really naive, aren't you, Haruki? It's not like I said I'd dump you or anything～"

findings.highlight: emptiness in my stomach that goes hand in hand with an appetite
findings.evidenceJa: 食欲の伴わない空腹感
findings.explanation: Haruki is left with hunger unaccompanied by appetite, a dangerous symptom of his fever and collapse. The English says the hunger goes hand in hand with an appetite, reversing the symptom immediately before he considers an ambulance.
findings.japanese: 後に残るは更なる疲れと、食欲の伴わない空腹感。
findings.todokanai: What I'm left with is an even greater fatigue and the sensation of emptiness in my stomach that goes hand in hand with an appetite.

findings.highlight: I'm unquestionably hallucinating right now
findings.evidenceJa: 頭がぼうっとしてたからに違いない
findings.explanation: Haruki says his head must have been foggy, explaining why he opened the door without checking the intercom. The English turns ordinary feverish dazedness into an unequivocal hallucination, inventing a much more severe mental symptom.
findings.japanese: 頭がぼうっとしてたからに違いない。
findings.todokanai: I'm unquestionably hallucinating right now.

findings.highlight: blurting out an answer for a question that hasn't even been asked yet
findings.evidenceJa: 質問よりも先に答えを言われてしまうなんて
findings.explanation: Setsuna answers Haruki's 'Why?' before he can formulate the full question, another sign that his feverish mind is slow. The English says Haruki himself blurted out an answer before a question, reversing the speaker and the conversational joke.
findings.japanese:
やっぱり、頭がぼうっとしてたからに違いない。
質問よりも先に答えを言われてしまうなんて。
findings.todokanai: As I thought, I'm unquestionably hallucinating right now. What am I doing, blurting out an answer for a question that hasn't even been asked yet?

findings.highlight: slowly satisfying my intense hunger
findings.evidenceJa: 猛烈な空腹感が、けれどゆっくりとせり上がってきた
findings.explanation: Once his stomach begins working, an intense hunger slowly wells up in Haruki. The English says the food is slowly satisfying that hunger, reversing the physiological recovery which explains why he immediately asks for more.
findings.japanese:
心配していた胃からの猛烈な拒絶反応もなく、
それどころか、きちんと活動を始めてくれたようで、
猛烈な空腹感が、けれどゆっくりとせり上がってきた。
findings.todokanai: My concerns of my stomach's vehement rejection of her food have thankfully been baseless. Contrarily, my stomach's starting to work properly, slowly satisfying my intense hunger.

findings.highlight: it hurts more to hear that the past was more painful and harsh than the present
findings.evidenceJa: あの時辛かった、苦しかったって言われる方が、たった今辛い、苦しいって言われるより、わたしには辛くて、苦しい
findings.explanation: Setsuna says it hurts her more to be told after the fact, 'I was suffering then,' than to be told in the moment, 'I'm suffering now.' The English instead compares whether the past itself was harsher than the present, losing her plea that Haruki ask for help while she can still act.
findings.japanese:
「あの時辛かった、苦しかったって言われる方が、
たった今辛い、苦しいって言われるより、
わたしには辛くて、苦しいんだからね？」
findings.todokanai: "Personally, I think it hurts more to hear that the past was more painful and harsh than the present, you know?"

findings.highlight: the cooking I treated Kazusa to three years prior
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前、初めて俺とかずさに料理を振舞ってくれた時
findings.explanation: Haruki compares Setsuna's present skill with the first meal Setsuna cooked for both him and Kazusa three years earlier. The English makes Haruki the cook who treated Kazusa, reversing the actor and breaking the callback to Setsuna's first attempt to feed the trio.
findings.japanese:
三年前、初めて俺とかずさに料理を振舞ってくれた時と
比べても、きっちりと三年分の進歩が見て取れるくらい、
腕が上がってた。
findings.todokanai: Even if I compare this to the cooking I treated Kazusa to three years prior, there's definitely been enough improvement in these three years that I can grasp it.

findings.highlight: "Then why don't we talk a little more today? Or are you tired of listening to me?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「じゃあ、今日のうちにもう少しだけ話をしたいな。
わたしの話、聞く気ないかな？」
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether Chiaki would be willing to listen to her story; the English asks whether Chiaki is tired of listening to her.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ、今日のうちにもう少しだけ話をしたいな。
わたしの話、聞く気ないかな？」
findings.todokanai: "Then why don't we talk a little more today? Or are you tired of listening to me?"

findings.highlight: what I've done to him… and how I ended up ruining everything
findings.evidenceJa: あたしが彼に何をしてあげたか…そして、何をしでかしたか
findings.explanation: Chiaki promises to tell Setsuna both what she did for Haruki and what she did to him—the aid and the transgression in deliberate opposition. The English renders both as harm and adds that she ruined everything, prejudging the morally mixed account she is about to perform.
findings.japanese:
「いいよ、教えてあげる。
あたしが彼に何をしてあげたか…
そして、何をしでかしたか、をね」
findings.todokanai: "Fine, I'll tell you all about it. I'll tell you what I've done to him… and how I ended up ruining everything after that."

findings.highlight: the characters in Yuutsuru
findings.evidenceJa: 中学の大会で演じた“つう”
findings.explanation: Tsuu is the crane-wife role in Junji Kinoshita's canonical play The Twilight Crane. The English again leaves the work as unexplained romanization and describes plural characters, obscuring the specific famous role Chiaki places beside her Four Kashiwagi Sisters feat.
findings.japanese:
「中学の大会で演じた“つう”や、
付属祭で演じた“柏木四姉妹”と同じ、
一つの役なんだ」
findings.todokanai: "Much like how I single-handedly played the roles of the characters in Yuutsuru I performed in the middle school competition and The Four Kashiwagi Sisters during the high school festival."

findings.highlight: At the beginning of winter break
findings.evidenceJa: 冬休み明けに会ったとき
findings.explanation: Setsuna noticed Shouko's happiness when they met after winter break, following Chiaki's relationship with Haruki during the holiday. The English moves the meeting to the beginning of winter break, before the experience whose emotional trace Setsuna detected.
findings.japanese:
「冬休み明けに会ったとき…
絶対に、いつもの晶子さんじゃなかった」
findings.todokanai: "At the beginning of winter break… I'm absolutely sure that you weren't the usual Shouko-san."

findings.highlight: I was broken like that three years ago
findings.evidenceJa: わたしも三年前、壊したから
findings.explanation: Setsuna says that when women love the same man such things happen, and that she too broke things three years ago. The English says she was broken, reversing agent and victim and erasing the self-accusation through which Setsuna identifies with and forgives Chiaki.
findings.japanese:
「同じ人を好きになっちゃうと、そういうこともあるよ。
わたしも三年前、壊したから」
findings.todokanai: "For two people to fall in love with the same person… things like that happen. I was broken like that three years ago."

findings.highlight: Embracing a man who you don't even love
findings.evidenceJa: 好きでもない男の人に、簡単に抱かれることなんかできない
findings.explanation: Setsuna says a woman cannot easily let herself be taken or slept with by a man she does not love—some girls cannot do it even with a man they love. The English makes the woman the agent of an ordinary embrace, reversing grammatical direction and stripping the claim of its sexual stakes.
findings.japanese:
「好きでもない男の人に、
簡単に抱かれることなんかできないよ。
…好きでもできない女の子だっているのに」
findings.todokanai: "Embracing a man who you don't even love isn't something you can do. …Especially not when another girl who loves him can't bring herself to do it."

findings.highlight: I'm really sorry for you to have had to come over
findings.evidenceJa: 部屋に上げてしまって、ごめん
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for having let Setsuna into his room because accepting her care may lead him to repeat his betrayal. The English apologizes that she had to come over, shifting the burden from his guilty acceptance of intimacy to her inconvenience.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ、ごめん…
部屋に上げてしまって、ごめん…
本当は、優しくしてもらうべきじゃなかった」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I'm sorry… I'm really sorry for you to have had to come over to my apartment… You really shouldn't be treating me so nicely."

findings.highlight: to have been able to treat her as a woman all this time
findings.evidenceJa: これからもずっと女として扱えるのって、世界一ころっと騙された、俺くらいかなぁ
findings.explanation: Haruki wonders whether he, the world's biggest sucker, may be the only person who can keep treating Chiaki as a woman from now on. The English turns this into a completed past ability, losing the prospective commitment that reveals why he may still choose her.
findings.japanese:
「あいつのこと、
これからもずっと女として扱えるのって、
世界一ころっと騙された、俺くらいかなぁって」
findings.todokanai: "And to have been able to treat her as a woman all this time. I guess I'm the only person in the world that's this gullible."

findings.highlight: I'm not someone indispensable to her
findings.evidenceJa: あいつは俺が必要とするような奴じゃなかったのに
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki was never supposed to be the kind of person he would need, then asks whether he still loves and needs her. The English says he was not indispensable to Chiaki, reversing the direction of need and disrupting the progression to his separate hope that she may need him.
findings.japanese: あいつは俺が必要とするような奴じゃなかったのに。
findings.todokanai: Even though I'm aware that I'm not someone indispensable to her…
